definition: Policy approaches that focus on regulating or monitoring the computational resources (hardware, training compute) used to develop advanced AI systems.
details: Compute governance treats large-scale training compute as a useful policy lever, since it is a relatively measurable and controllable input to frontier AI development compared to algorithms or data.

explainer.lead: Compute governance uses the computing power behind advanced AI training as a point for oversight. It matters because large training runs require substantial hardware and computation, which can be easier to measure and control than the algorithms or data involved.

tiers.eli5: Training the biggest AI systems is a bit like running a huge factory with thousands of machines working for a long time. Compute governance means keeping track of those machines and their work, and sometimes setting rules about them. The idea is that watching the factory can be easier than inspecting every idea or piece of information used inside it.
tiers.practitioner: In practice, compute governance can be built around accounting for training runs and the hardware they use, with reporting or monitoring triggered at chosen scales. Engineers may need consistent records that connect hardware usage to particular development efforts. A key pitfall is treating a compute measurement as a complete assessment of an AI system, since it does not directly describe its algorithms, data, or behavior.
tiers.paperLevel: Let C denote the computational resources used in AI development, including hardware and training compute. Compute governance is the set of policies that regulate or monitor C as an input to advanced AI development. Its policy value rests on C being relatively measurable and controllable compared with algorithms or data, but governing this input does not by itself characterize or control every property of the resulting system.

explainer.example: Suppose a rule requires developers conducting sufficiently large training efforts to report the computing resources used. A developer training an advanced model would document its hardware and training compute, allowing the regulator to monitor that development effort through its computational footprint.
explainer.intuition: Frontier AI development needs inputs such as algorithms, data, and computation. Compute governance focuses on computation because large amounts of hardware and training compute form a comparatively visible handle for policy.
howItWorks: Identify the hardware and training compute used for AI development.
Measure or collect reports about those computational resources.
Apply monitoring or rules at relevant development scales.
Use the resulting oversight to manage large-scale training activity.
explainer.whyItMatters: It gives policymakers a way to oversee an important input to frontier AI development without having to directly control every algorithm or dataset. Its usefulness comes from the relative measurability and controllability of large-scale training compute.
misconceptions: It is not limited to regulating computer chips; training compute is also included.
Measuring compute is not the same as measuring an AI system's capabilities or risks.
It does not replace governance of algorithms or data.

diagram.caption: Compute governance turns information about hardware and training compute into a basis for policy oversight.
